title: Layer roles per copper-layer count (top to bottom). SIG = signals (with ground fill), GND = solid ground plane, PWR = power plane (or ground).
rules: Fast signals run over a solid ground plane, never across a split or void in it; TI does not recommend referencing high-speed signals to a power plane [SPRAAR7J 2.4].
A power plane next to a ground plane adds high-frequency bypass capacitance [SN75LVCP600S 11.1].

2.source: (derived) from SPRAAR7J 2.4: with two layers the only reference a top-layer signal can have is a ground fill on the bottom layer, kept as unbroken as the routing allows.

4.source: TI SN75LVCP600S datasheet 11.1 Layout Guidelines: at least four layers; a solid ground plane next to the high-speed signal layer, the power plane next to the ground plane.

6.source: TI SPRAAR7J High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines, Table 3-1 Example PCB Stackups (6-layer). The PWR layer is POWER/GROUND there; adjacent inner signal layers routed at 90 degrees to each other.

sources.SPRAAR7J: https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/SPRAAR7 (revision J, February 2023), section 2.4 and Table 3-1
